results.text: Conversation with Claude about planning the Japan trip, exported from Claude. We talked through the route again: Tokyo first, then Kanazawa, then Kyoto, all by rail on a seven-day pass plus single tickets. Tokyo: five nights near Kuramae, which is quieter than Shinjuku and close to the Sumida river for morning runs. I asked about vegetarian food in Tokyo; the suggestions were shojin ryori temples, a few Indian places and convenience-store onigiri with care about dashi. Kanazawa: we booked the ryokan Yamanoo for 9 to 11 April 2027, two nights, with a vegetarian kaiseki dinner arranged in advance. From Kanazawa we go to Kyoto on the Thunderbird and Shinkansen connection, about two and a half hours. Kyoto: four nights in a small guesthouse in Demachiyanagi, near the river. We considered a day trip to Nara but may skip it to keep the pace slow. Packing: light layers, a rain jacket, running shoes, and the camera with one lens. Budget check: accommodation is about half of what we planned to spend. Things to book later: the teamLab tickets in Tokyo and a cooking class in Kyoto. Remember to get a Suica card on the phone before leaving.

results.text:
Export from the Harbor accessibility walkthrough, 21 October 2026. Participants were Sam and two club volunteers using demonstration accounts. The session used the staging build and invented bookings, so no member records were copied into these notes. The volunteers first explored the calendar without coaching. Both found the day headings easy to scan, but one initially mistook the small dot below a date for a selected state. We recorded that observation for the next design review rather than changing the calendar during the session.

The next exercise covered reserving a dinghy and checking the confirmation screen. We tried the largest supported text size and landscape orientation on the borrowed test phone. Longer instructor names wrapped onto a second line without covering the time. The booking summary remained readable, although the gap above the cancellation explanation looked larger than intended. Sam captured a screenshot using a fictional instructor name. The volunteers asked whether the summary could repeat the boat name near the final button; that suggestion went into the review list.

After a short break, we repeated the same flow with VoiceOver. The reading order moved from the date to the available times and then to the instructor choices. One volunteer used headphones while the other followed the screen. We noted where the spoken labels were longer than the visible text and checked that the distinction was meaningful.
